title: Window Functions
tagline: OVER clause — analytics without GROUP BY collapse

options: Window function keeps all rows; aggregate collapses rows
Window function only works with ORDER BY
placementQuiz.explain: Window functions compute per-row using a window of rows; aggregates collapse groups into one row.

options: Window = all rows in result set
placementQuiz.explain: Empty OVER() = entire result set as single window partition.

placementQuiz.q: PARTITION BY dept_id in OVER clause:
options: Groups rows by dept_id and collapses them
Creates separate windows per dept_id; function computes within each
placementQuiz.explain: PARTITION BY splits result into independent windows per partition value.

options: ROW_NUMBER = 1,2,3...; RANK skips ties (1,2,2,4); DENSE_RANK no skip (1,2,2,3)
placementQuiz.explain: ROW_NUMBER always unique sequential. RANK skips on ties. DENSE_RANK no gaps.
Window functions only allowed in SELECT and ORDER BY clauses (not WHERE/HAVING).

placementQuiz.q: Default window frame when ORDER BY is present:
options: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING TO CURRENT ROW
placementQuiz.explain: Default = RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING TO CURRENT ROW. Includes all rows up to current row.

placementQuiz.q: LAG(salary, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) for first row returns:
placementQuiz.explain: Default value 0 used when no previous row exists.

blocks.md: A window function looks at a 'window' of rows around each row. PARTITION BY slices the data; ORDER BY arranges rows within each slice; frame clauses (ROWS/RANGE) define the window boundaries.

before.example: OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary)

blocks.md: Think of a spreadsheet: each row gets a new column computed from its 'window' of peer rows. PARTITION BY = filter to same department. ORDER BY = sort by salary. The function then computes over that window.

items: Window functions ONLY in SELECT and ORDER BY clauses
ORDER BY in OVER = defines row sequence for ranking/frame
Default frame: RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING TO CURRENT ROW

blocks.label: row_number
blocks.code:
-- Number rows within each department by salary desc
SELECT 
  name,
  dept_id,
  salary,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn
FROM employees;

-- Top 3 per department
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn
  FROM employees
) t WHERE rn <= 3;

blocks.label: rank
blocks.code:
-- RANK: ties get same rank, next rank skipped
SELECT 
  name,
  salary,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rnk
FROM employees;

-- Salaries: 100k, 100k, 90k → RANKs: 1, 1, 3

blocks.label: dense_rank
blocks.code:
-- DENSE_RANK: ties same rank, no skip
SELECT 
  name,
  salary,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS drnk
FROM employees;

-- Salaries: 100k, 100k, 90k → DENSE_RANKs: 1, 1, 2

items.explain: RANK: ties share rank, next rank skips. 100k tied at 1, next is 3.
DENSE_RANK: ties share rank, next rank continues. 100k=1, 90k=2.

items.q: ROW_NUMBER() with PARTITION BY dept_id, ORDER BY salary DESC for 3 employees in dept 1 with salaries 100k, 90k, 80k:
items.explain: ROW_NUMBER always unique sequential: highest salary = 1, second = 2, third = 3.

sections.title: Navigation Functions — LAG, LEAD, FIRST_VALUE, LAST_VALUE

blocks.label: lag lead
blocks.code:
-- LAG: previous row's value
SELECT 
  sale_date,
  amount,
  LAG(amount) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS prev_amount,
  LAG(amount, 2) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS two_days_ago
FROM daily_sales;

-- LEAD: next row's value
SELECT 
  sale_date,
  amount,
  LEAD(amount) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS next_amount
FROM daily_sales;

-- With default value
SELECT 
  sale_date,
  amount,
  LAG(amount, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS prev_amount
FROM daily_sales;

blocks.label: first_value last_value
blocks.code:
-- FIRST_VALUE: first in window
SELECT 
  dept_id,
  name,
  salary,
  FIRST_VALUE(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS dept_max
FROM employees;

-- LAST_VALUE needs explicit frame!
SELECT 
  dept_id,
  name,
  salary,
  LAST_VALUE(salary) OVER (
    PARTITION BY dept_id ORDER BY salary DESC
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
  ) AS dept_min
FROM employees;
blocks.pg: -- LAST_VALUE needs explicit frame (default frame excludes following rows)
blocks.mysql: -- MySQL 8.0+: FIRST_VALUE, LAST_VALUE with frame clause

blocks.md: **LAST_VALUE default frame = RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING TO CURRENT ROW.** Always specify ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING for true last value.

items.q: LAG(salary, 1) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) for first row returns:
items.explain: No previous row → NULL. Use LAG(salary, 1, 0) for default 0.
Default frame = CURRENT ROW. LAST_VALUE = current row. Need explicit frame.

revisionCard: Window function = per-row computation over window; keeps all rows
PARTITION BY = slices data; ORDER BY = sequences rows; frame = window boundaries
ROW_NUMBER = unique 1..N; RANK skips on ties; DENSE_RANK no gaps
LAG/LEAD = previous/next row; FIRST_VALUE/LAST_VALUE need frame clause
Window functions only in SELECT/ORDER BY; use CTE/subquery for WHERE/HAVING
Default frame: RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING TO CURRENT ROW

glossary.def: Computes value per row using a window of rows defined by OVER clause.
Divides result into partitions; function computed independently per partition.
ROWS/RANGE BETWEEN ... defines window boundaries relative to current row.
Access previous/next row value in window.
